title: kirándul, piknikezik, sportol: Weekend Verbs in the Past

sections.title: Old verbs, one new tense
sections.content: You already know kirándul, piknikezik and sportol from talking about weekend plans. They follow exactly the pattern from the last lesson — including piknikezik, which is another -ik verb that drops its -ik completely and conjugates like any other verb once you're in the past tense.

items.english: We hiked a lot last weekend.

items.spanish: Károly és Ildikó piknikeztek a parkban.
items.english: Károly and Ildikó had a picnic in the park.

items.spanish: Zsófia és Tamás sokat sportoltak a hétvégén.
items.english: Zsófia and Tamás did a lot of sport over the weekend.

sections.content: kirándul and sportol both end in -l, so like tanul they never need a linking vowel, not even in 3rd person singular: kirándult, sportolt. piknikezik ends in -z, so like dolgozik it takes bare -t- everywhere except 3rd person singular, where it needs -ett-: piknikezett.
